**BREAKING: 40 Ohio Children Dead After Receiving Contaminated MMR Vaccine Batch; CDC and FBI Launch Emergency Probe**

**By Alicia Renner, Investigative Health Correspondent**

COLUMBUS, Ohio — At least 40 children across Ohio have died within 72 hours of receiving a routine measles-mumps-rubella vaccine from a single production lot, state health records and hospital officials confirmed Thursday, triggering an emergency federal investigation and a nationwide pause on the batch.

The children, ranging in age from 12 months to 6 years, developed high fevers, violent seizures, and rapid multi-organ failure shortly after vaccination, according to internal reports from the Ohio Department of Health and multiple children’s hospitals. The deaths span at least 17 counties, with the highest concentration in Franklin, Cuyahoga, Montgomery, and Hamilton counties.

“She was laughing in the pediatrician’s office. By midnight she was burning up with a fever of 106, and by 7 a.m. she was gone,” said Maria Delgado of Dayton, whose 18-month-old daughter received the shot Monday. “They told me the vaccine would protect her. It killed her.”

The Ohio Department of Health has ordered all healthcare providers to immediately quarantine lot **MMR-7C42-X9**, manufactured by Merck at its West Point, Pennsylvania facility in March 2024 and distributed to at least 41 states. The CDC and FDA have activated emergency operations centers, and FBI agents have joined the investigation amid early indications of possible manufacturing contamination or tampering.

Preliminary toxicology reports from the Franklin County Coroner’s Office found “unidentified particulate matter” in unopened vials from the same lot, as well as “abnormal levels of an unknown compound” in several of the deceased children, according to a source with direct knowledge of the findings. An internal hospital memo obtained by this outlet warns staff to “treat all patients who received MMR lot 7C42-X9 as potential critical cases” and to prepare for additional fatalities.

At Nationwide Children’s Hospital in Columbus, 14 of the deaths occurred. A pediatric intensive care physician, speaking on condition of anonymity because he was not authorized to discuss the matter publicly, described the clinical course as “unprecedented.”

“These are previously healthy kids. They come in seizing. Their livers and kidneys shut down. Nothing we do stops it,” the physician said. “We’ve never seen anything like this in a vaccine-related event. This is not a normal adverse reaction.”

Merck issued a brief statement saying it is “cooperating fully with authorities” and has “paused distribution of the lot out of an abundance of caution.” The company declined to answer questions about whether the batch had passed required sterility and contamination testing prior to release.

The CDC has scheduled an emergency meeting of the Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices for Friday and has asked clinicians and public health agencies in all states that received the lot to suspend use immediately. The agency said it “cannot rule out additional cases” outside Ohio.

A leaked internal email from the Ohio Department of Health’s immunization program manager instructed local health departments: “Do not discuss lot numbers or potential contamination with the public. Direct all inquiries to the communications office.” The email, first reported by this outlet, has drawn accusations of a cover-up from grieving parents and some state lawmakers.

Governor Mike DeWine is expected to declare a public health emergency and address the state Thursday evening. Meanwhile, hospitals and urgent care centers across Ohio report a surge of frightened parents seeking guidance and refusing all childhood vaccines.

“They told us vaccines are completely safe. My son is dead because I trusted them,” said David Okafor of Cleveland, whose 4-year-old died Tuesday night. “How many more children have to die before someone tells the truth?”

The CDC is urging anyone in possession of MMR lot **MMR-7C42-X9** to report it immediately and not administer any remaining doses. The agency acknowledged that additional deaths may be reported in the coming days.

This is a developing story. Check back for updates.
